# Contrast audit

Spec §7: *"WCAG AA contrast on every text/panel pair, verified not assumed."*

Every ratio below was **computed** from the hex values in `src/styles/tokens.css` by
`tools/contrast.mjs`, using the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula. None of them is typed in.
Change a token and these numbers change; put a pair under its threshold and the build stops.

**Thresholds.** Body text (under 24px, or under 19px semibold) needs **4.5:1**. Large text
(24px and up, or 19px and up semibold) needs **3:1**. A non-text mark that carries meaning — a
hairline, a focus ring, a border — needs **3:1** under WCAG 1.4.11.

**Rows marked `info`** are measured deliberately and are excluded from the pass/fail gate.
They record *why* a rule exists. The ore rows are the reason ore is never a glyph.

## What is not measured here, and why

- **Terrain colours against each other.** The terrain is a picture, not text. §7 requires AA on
  every *text/panel* pair, and every text/panel pair is in the tables above. The terrain never
  carries a glyph: §7 puts all body text on opaque panels precisely so the background cannot
  reduce contrast.
- **Text over the canvas.** There is none, by the same rule. If a component ever draws text
  directly on the terrain, that is a §7 violation before it is a contrast problem.
- **Colour as the only signal.** Not a ratio, so not this file's job. The rule the components
  hold to instead: every ore mark has a non-colour partner — a border position, a label, or a
  glyph.

_42 pairs measured across 2 themes._
